newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African exchange grants listing for INCA bonds.
newsitem.headline: S.African exchange grants listing for INCA bonds.

text.p: South Africa's Infrastructure Finance Corp (INCA) had been granted a listing of three bonds worth 1.2 billion rand, the Bond Exchange said on Monday.

The offering of the three bonds -- the IN01, IN02 and IN03 -- opens at 0700 GMT on Tuesday and closes at 1100 GMT on the same day. Pricing and allotment results are expected to be announced by 1100 GMT on Wednesday.

The exchange said the 200 million rand IN01 bond, redeemable on June 30, 2003 and which carries a 13.5 percent coupon, would be pegged at 75 basis points above the closing rate of government's R162 on Monday.
The 800 million rand IN02 bond, which matures on June 30, 2006 and also carries a 13.5 percent coupon, would be pegged at 80 basis points above the closing R150 rate on Monday.
Some 500 million rand of this bond will be for private placement.
The 200 million rand IN03 bond, which carries a 14.00 percent coupon and will be redeemable on June 30, 2011, will be pegged at 80 basis points above the closing rate of the R153 on Monday.
Interest dates for all three bonds are June 30 and December 31 of each year, while books close on June 1 and December 1.
The INCA bonds will be immobilised in the central depository and settlement will take place through the Bond Exchange's electronic nett settlement system. First settlement will take place on March 6.

INCA, set up last October to help fund infrastructure projects, intends to raise 12 billion rand over the next seven years in a process which will join the private sector and government in addressing the country's infrastructure backlog.
Government estimates put South Africa's total infrastructure needs at 171 billion rand over the next five years.
INCA, whose principal partners are First National Bank, the Commonwealth Development Corp and Southern Life, has a domestic long-term rating of "AA-" from European rating agency IBCA.
